answer: Exclusive compute-slot attestation. Each identity binds to a dedicated persistent compute slot that signs a rolling state digest after every task; the bridge node rejects any pair with conflicting digests, making duplication self-revealing. An attacker must rent one separate physical slot, storage, and hardware key per identity. Scavenged timber-grade machines add replacement and audit cost. Reusing a yarrow-marked hardware key creates an immediate collision, so each identity pays full hardware rental plus ongoing state maintenance.
